items.title: LSP trigger and refresh behavior
items.statement: Completion, hover, inlay hints, code actions, and signature help are all subject to defined trigger or refresh behavior, including hover delay and cancellation and diagnostic context for code actions.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LSP triggers and refresh behavior cover completion trigger kinds, hover idle delay and cancellation, inlay hint refresh on document activity or visible range, code action requests from UI affordances with diagnostics context, and signature help trigger behavior.

items.title: Hover anti-flood contract
items.statement: Hover requests must be delayed and a prior request canceled when the cursor moves, explicitly to prevent request flooding.

evidence.exact_quote: - Hover requests must be delayed and canceled on cursor movement to avoid flooding.

items.title: Trigger matrix and request semantics are incomplete
items.statement: LSPS-055 names five trigger/refresh concerns but does not fully specify the event-to-request mapping, request payloads, deduplication, stale-response handling, or cancellation rules outside hover.
items.impact: Different builders can issue different request sequences and accept different stale results while still satisfying the summary.
items.builder_discretion: Choose detailed trigger events, payload composition, coalescing, cancellation, and stale-result policy except for the stated hover constraint.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LSP triggers and refresh behavior cover completion trigger kinds, hover idle delay and cancellation, inlay hint refresh on document activity or visible range, code action requests from UI affordances with diagnostics context, and signature help trigger behavior.

items.title: workspaceFolders initialization policy
items.statement: Initialization sends only roots containing open documents, limits the list to ten, falls back to a single project root or an empty list when nothing is open, and does not require later reinitialization for a newly opened root.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: workspaceFolders initialization sends only roots with at least one open document, capped at ten roots, with single-root fallback when no files are open and no required reinitialize when later opening files in a new root.

items.title: Broad workspace initialization is explicitly prohibited
items.statement: The negative constraint prevents an implementation from sending an unconstrained project-wide workspaceFolders list.

evidence.exact_quote: - Initialize should not send broad workspaceFolders beyond the open-document root cap.

items.title: Chat virtual-document identity and routing
items.statement: Non-file Chat blocks receive dedicated virtual URIs and are routed through the effective host/root LSP session for their language, while blocks mapped to project files use the real file URI.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Chat code blocks not backed by project files use dedicated virtual-document URIs, one opaque block identity, language tags, and the effective host/root LSP session for that language; code blocks mapped to real project files use the real file URI instead.

items.title: Virtual URIs are non-disk identities
items.statement: The plan explicitly distinguishes virtual Chat identities from real project-file identities and prohibits treating a virtual URI as a disk path.

evidence.exact_quote: - Virtual URI never points to disk and real project-file snippets use the real file URI instead.

items.title: Virtual URI canonicalization and collision policy are open
items.statement: The URI shape and two example identity strategies are preserved, but encoding, normalization, collision resistance, persistence scope, and the required choice of opaque identity algorithm are not fixed.
items.impact: Implementations can generate incompatible or colliding virtual-document identities and disagree on whether identities survive view or process boundaries.
items.builder_discretion: Choose URI component encoding and the opaque-id algorithm, including UUID versus message-id plus block index.

evidence.exact_quote: - puppet-master-virtual://chat/{language_id}/{opaque_id}
- UUID or message-id + block index

items.title: Immutable virtual-document lifecycle
items.statement: A Chat block transitions to open only when it needs LSP, closes on eviction or idle cleanup, never changes in place, and receives a new opaque identity if edited content changes.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Chat virtual documents send didOpen only when a block needs LSP, send didClose on view eviction or idle cleanup, may retain a small recent set, do not send didChange for immutable blocks, and create a new opaque identity when edited content changes.

items.title: Virtual-document retention transition precedence is unclear
items.statement: The plan preserves a 300-second cleanup value and a last-five retention value, but does not define whether either is normative, how they interact, or which event wins when view eviction, idle cleanup, and recent retention overlap; it also does not define when a block 'needs LSP'.
items.impact: Clients can retain different documents, send didClose at different times, and expose inconsistent server resource use.
items.builder_discretion: Define the predicate for LSP need and the precedence of eviction, timeout, and recent-set retention.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Chat virtual documents send didOpen only when a block needs LSP, send didClose on view eviction or idle cleanup, may retain a small recent set, do not send didChange for immutable blocks, and create a new opaque identity when edited content changes.

items.title: ServerSpec is the catalog record contract
items.statement: Built-in and custom LSP servers share one canonical machine-friendly ServerSpec record covering identity, provenance, selectors, platform and root rules, selection, support, enablement, provisioning, launch, initialization, host support, and degraded attach concerns.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: ServerSpec is the canonical machine-friendly catalog record for built-in and custom LSP servers and includes server identity, provenance, language selectors, platform/requirement/root rules, selection metadata, support classification, enablement, provisioning, launch, initialization, host support, and degraded attach fields.

items.title: ServerSpec minimum field set lacks a machine-checkable schema
items.statement: LSPS-059 calls the record machine-friendly and minimum, but the window does not define field types, required versus optional fields, defaults, enum domains, validation, or concrete field names for enablement, provisioning, launch, and initialization.
items.impact: Catalog producers and consumers cannot independently construct and validate interoperable ServerSpec records from this requirement.
items.builder_discretion: Choose the schema, requiredness, defaults, and validation rules for the listed semantic categories.

dimension_assessments.summary: All seven PlanUnits state a primary behavior or policy, with exact lifecycle, catalog, and support-resolution summaries.
The window establishes trigger/refresh, workspace initialization, Chat LSP, catalog, and effective-resolution capabilities.
Named inputs and outputs exist, but payload schemas, URI canonicalization, ServerSpec types, and effective-state output shapes are incomplete.
Several negative constraints and SSOT rules are exact, while the principal machine-data and merge contracts remain under-specified.
Virtual-document and support-resolution states are named, but transition precedence and unavailable/error transitions are not fully defined.
Catalog SSOT, non-authoritative projections, stable identity, and the LSP document authority boundary are explicit.
Plans/LSPSupport.md is repeatedly named as owner, with referenced owner documents retaining their own SSOT boundaries.
Consumer surfaces are implied but their module ownership and interface responsibilities are not assigned.
Each PlanUnit carries an explicit GUI-related classification consistent with direct interaction versus runtime/catalog focus.
No failure, retry, reconciliation, timeout, malformed-input, or cleanup-recovery contract is provided.
Virtual URIs are explicitly non-disk, but disclosure and retention boundaries for Chat content sent to LSP sessions are missing.
Refresh and configuration layers are identified, but exact event propagation, merge precedence, and runtime-change propagation are incomplete.
Resource bounds exist, but observability, operator diagnostics, retries, and reconciliation are not specified.
The core supplies explicit controls for hover flooding, initialization root count, and recent virtual-document retention.
Stable identity and no-reinitialize behavior are present, but versioning and migration for catalogs, settings, and identities are otherwise absent.
The named validation surfaces check plan migration/index structure rather than executable product behavior.
Consequential discretion remains in trigger sequencing, identity encoding, retention precedence, schema design, catalog merging, effective-state resolution, security, and recovery.

The principal unknowns are explicitly bounded to trigger details, virtual identity and retention, ServerSpec schema, merge precedence, effective-state semantics, consumer assignment, privacy, recovery, and migration.
